speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Transport in 2023 (a) what is the number of times public transport commuters who were charged twice for the same bus or MRT trip because they used a different SimplyGo device or card for their entry and exit; (b) what was the total amount charged; (c) how many applications for refunds were made; (d) how many applications were acceded to; and (e) what was the total amount refunded.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether the Ministry will consider providing educational materials and instructional procedures to commuters (i) to avoid using different devices or cards when entering and exiting buses and MRTs and (ii) to apply for refunds should any double charging occur; and (b) whether fare gates can prevent commuters from exiting if they attempt to use a different device or card from the ones they used during entry.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If a commuter taps in with one device or card, and taps out with a different device or card, two separate transactions are recorded.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This can occur for a variety of reasons.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For example, a commuter may have multiple cards in their wallet and tapping the entire wallet at the reader could result in different cards being detected at entry and exit.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: A commuter may also have used a different device, such as a smartphone, smartwatch, or physical bank card, to tap in and tap out.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As the digital identifier of each device or card is different, even if they are linked to the same bank card, these are also recorded as separate transactions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The vast majority of transactions in public transport are carried out accurately with commuters using the same card or device to tap in and out.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is the same latency problem for account-based ticketing systems that prevents fare deduction and card balance information from being displayed immediately at fare gates and bus card readers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These errors can be avoided, by using the same device or card to tap in and tap out.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is why other public transport systems like in London and Hong Kong who face similar issues have taken steps to raise awareness among commuters to reduce such occurrences.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will continue with these publicity efforts to raise awareness among commuters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Commuters can check their transactions using the SimplyGo app or at ticket machines.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If they find transactions which are wrongly computed, they can apply for a refund via the app, or seek assistance at ticket offices.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: First, are the commuters charged the maximum fare twice, if they use the same device linked to the same SimplyGo account for tapping in and tapping out?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, from what I observed, I hear the Minister say that there are posters put up and I do notice those posters, but I notice that they are mostly only in English.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can they also be published in different languages so that all commuters are aware of this issue?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, I would like to thank Mr Giam for raising these two Parliamentary Questions and also for his supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is an important initiative that we want to raise awareness for.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We use this opportunity to let more commuters know that the best way to avoid this issue from cropping up in the first place is to use the same device or to use the same card.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But Mr Giam is right that errors do occur.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is why it is important for us to look at how we can improve the system design where possible to make the refunding process easier, more convenient.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I will certainly take on board his suggestion as we look at how to enhance SimplyGo's overall system design and user experience.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Which is what we wanted to do for the project as a whole, but I will also pay attention to this particular aspect; in case there are some fares that need to be refunded, we will see what is the process to allow that to happen in a more convenient manner.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I will also take on board Mr Giam's suggestion for the languages on the posters so that we are able to reach out to more commuters and to raise awareness.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For Mr Giam's first question, it depends on whether you are referring to rail or bus because the calculations are slightly different.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, not quite the maximum, but quite close to the maximum.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But as I mentioned earlier, I think the best way to protect commuters against such occurrences is to raise awareness and help them to avoid this in the first place by using the same device or the same card.
